questions.prompt: Put the steps of a conditional `GET` with `ETag` in order.
steps: The server replies `200 OK` with the body and `ETag: "a1b2c3d4"`
The resource is unchanged, so the server replies `304 Not Modified` with an empty body
questions.explanation: `ETag` fingerprints the resource; the client echoes it back in `If-None-Match`, and if nothing changed the server sends `304` without re-sending the data.

questions.prompt: Two users edit the same task at once, and the second `PUT` silently overwrites the first. Which headers fix this "lost update"?
options: `ETag` plus `If-Match`, with the server answering `412 Precondition Failed` if the resource changed
`If-None-Match`, with the server answering `304 Not Modified`
questions.explanation: The client sends the `ETag` it last read in `If-Match`; if the resource has changed since, the server rejects the write with `412 Precondition Failed`.

questions.prompt: What is the difference between `Cache-Control: no-store` and `Cache-Control: no-cache`?
options: `no-cache` means never cache; `no-store` means cache for one hour
`no-store` caches per user; `no-cache` caches across users
`no-store` means never cache; `no-cache` means cache but revalidate every time
questions.explanation: `no-store` is for data that must never be cached, such as sensitive per-user data; `no-cache` allows caching but forces revalidation on every use.

questions.prompt: Why is it useful for a server to send `WWW-Authenticate` with a `401` response?
options: It tells the browser to switch to HTTPS
It grants the client a new token automatically
It lets the client tell "no token" apart from "token expired" or "wrong scheme", for example to trigger a refresh-token flow
It tells the client how many seconds to wait before retrying
questions.explanation: `WWW-Authenticate` names the scheme the client should use and can carry details such as `error="invalid_token"`, so a well-behaved client knows whether to refresh its token.

questions.prompt: What is the difference between the `Content-Type` and `Accept` headers?
options: `Content-Type` declares the media type of the body being sent; `Accept` lists the response formats the client can handle
`Content-Type` is only for responses; `Accept` is only for errors
`Accept` declares the body's format; `Content-Type` lists the languages the client prefers
Both declare the request body's format; `Accept` is the older name
questions.explanation: `Content-Type` describes the body of a request or response; `Accept` is the client saying which formats it wants back, and the server can answer `406 Not Acceptable` if it can produce none.
